key_insight: Fe and Cr substitution at Ni grain-boundary planes increases cohesion, with effects that depend on the alloying element and local atomic structure.
engineering_relevance: Validated atomistic cohesion estimates could inform continuum fracture models for multicomponent Ni-based alloys.
method: Compute DFT rigid-body separation curves for six symmetric-tilt Ni grain boundaries.
Extract work of separation and maximum traction using the universal binding energy relation.
Benchmark ML interatomic foundation models against DFT, then use a validated model to sample finer alloying increments and ternary compositions.
evidence_signal: One tested ML model quantitatively reproduces DFT work of separation and maximum traction; ternary Ni56Fe20Cr24 calculations probe combined Fe–Cr effects.
watch_item: Binary alloying trends do not quantitatively capture Fe–Cr interplay, so explicit ternary calculations remain necessary.
paper_title: Alloying effects on the interface cohesion of grain boundaries in the Ni--Fe--Cr system
